# Signed-note and checkpoint fixtures

Test data for `src/note.rs` (C2SP `signed-note`, `tlog-checkpoint` and
`tlog-cosignature`).

## `vectors.json`

Generated by `generate.go`, which uses only the Go standard library:

```sh
go run generate.go > vectors.json
```

The signatures come from Go's `crypto/ed25519`, so they are independent of
the Rust code under test, and the key IDs, verifier keys (vkeys), signature
lines and `cosignature/v1` messages are built in the generator directly from
the specifications. Ed25519 signing is deterministic and every key is derived
from a fixed, public seed (`SHA-256("pragmatic signed-note fixture: " +
label)`), so rerunning the generator reproduces the file byte for byte. These
keys sign nothing but this test data.

Before writing, the generator verifies every case with Go's verifier and
exits if its own result disagrees with the expected one.

The file has two parts:

- `keys`: five verifier keys, each with its label, name, signature type
  (`1` = Ed25519 note signature, `4` = Ed25519 `cosignature/v1`), key ID,
  public key and vkey text. `witness1-plain` is the first witness's name and
  public key registered as a type `1` key, which has a different key ID.
- `cases`: a signed note, the checkpoint its text should parse to (`null`
  when the text is not a checkpoint), the labels of the keys to trust, and
  the expected result:
  - `ok`, with `verified` listing each trusted key that verified, once, in
    signature-line order, with the index of its first line and, for
    cosignatures, the signed timestamp;
  - `invalid_signature`: a line from a trusted key fails to verify;
  - `repeated_key`: a trusted key signed two different lines, which
    `tlog-checkpoint` forbids;
  - `no_verified_signature`: no trusted key signed.

  Lines are checked in order, and the first failing line decides the
  result.

The cases cover a log signature alone; a log signature with two witness
cosignatures under different trust sets; unknown signers; a flipped
signature bit from a trusted and from an untrusted key; a cosignature whose
timestamp field was changed; a cosigner key configured as a plain Ed25519
key; the log's name and key ID on another key's signature; a cosignature
over a different checkpoint; extension lines; the empty tree; a repeated
log signature line and a repeated cosignature line; two valid cosignatures
from one witness with different timestamps, in both orders and with the
witness untrusted; and a note whose text is not a checkpoint and contains a
blank line.

## `sum.golang.org.note`

A real checkpoint from the Go checksum database, fetched from
`https://sum.golang.org/latest` on 2026-10-13 and stored unmodified. The test
verifies it with the key built into the `go` command
(`src/cmd/go/internal/modfetch/key.go`):

```
sum.golang.org+033de0ae+Ac4zctda0e5eza+HJyk9SxEdh+s3Ux18htTTAD8OuAn8
```

Its origin, `go.sum database tree`, contains spaces, which is why
`Checkpoint::parse` only requires the origin line to be non-empty.
`Checkpoint::encode` refuses to write such an origin, since `tlog-cosignature`
now forbids spaces in origins.

## Vectors in the test source

`src/note.rs` also checks the `PeterNeumann` and `EnochRoot` vectors from
Go's `golang.org/x/mod/sumdb/note` tests (BSD-style license, copyright The
Go Authors) and the examples in the C2SP `signed-note` and `tlog-checkpoint`
specifications.
